correctness.rationale: The scalar denominator is positive on the Laplacian spectrum, so the inverse is positive definite (in particular its diagonal is positive), and fixes the all-ones vector. Thus entrywise nonnegativity, a discrete min/max principle and sup-norm contractivity are equivalent. Multiplication of scalar series gives r(z)=1−z+z²/2−z⁴/4+O(z⁵). At distance four the first nonzero Laplacian power entry occurs at power four and is +1, from the unique geodesic. The two-vertex case follows from r(2h)<1; projection onto constant, leaf-difference and hub-versus-leaves subspaces gives the star formulas, with strict convexity of r ensuring positive leaf–leaf entries. Every diameter-three tree is a double star. The four-cell Laplacian is symmetric in the class-size weighted inner product and is a restriction of the original positive semidefinite operator. Its Padé denominator has positive determinant. Cross-cell inverse entries per vertex are quotient entries divided by destination cell size; same-leaf off-diagonals are the difference between the quotient diagonal entry and r(h), divided by class size, by the eigenvalue-one leaf-difference action. I reconstructed all eight numerator polynomials from alternating permutation sums for determinants and cofactors, verified exact leaf-count divisibility, and compared every rational monomial coefficient with the frozen certificate. All coefficients are strictly positive, with counts 18,22,15,15,22,10,28,28 and minimum h-degrees 1,1,2,2,1,4,2,2. This verifies the infinite positive direction, not just samples.
residual_risks: Negative entries on diameter-four-or-larger trees are proved for sufficiently small h, not uniformly over all h. No weighted, directed, or cyclic-graph classification follows.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier Resultary formula specializes exactly via the unique tree geodesic and proves necessity. It does not give sufficiency, which hinges on all-step control of the weighted four-cell restriction and the leaf-difference contributions.

evidence: The tree map is exactly r02(hQ) with Q=−L_T in Itkin–Kazbek's generator convention. Remark 4 distinguishes it from inverse M-matrix resolvent positivity and notes that it need not be unconditionally positive on Metzler generators.
Since rows sum to one, nonnegativity and maximum-norm contractivity are equivalent here; the tree result was compared under both formulations.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Resolvent positivity for a first-degree denominator is not the same map. A general sufficient large-step theorem does not establish contractivity at all positive steps or identify the correct tree family.

originality.rationale: The distance-four obstruction is exactly covered on trees by the earlier all-graph obstruction and is explicitly not claimed as new. The independently assessed distinct contribution is strict all-step positivity of all double stars, including arbitrarily unequal and unbounded leaf counts, and hence the exact all-tree diameter classification. No inspected covering statement supplies this positive direction.

value.rationale: The all-step maximum principle is a natural structural requirement for a graph heat update. The result supplies a sharp topology test on the full class of trees: the known local obstruction becomes necessary and sufficient because every double star, even highly unbalanced, passes uniformly. This is useful beyond the already-known path obstruction or any finite census.
residual_risks: The classification is for unweighted trees and this Padé order only.
